rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Disclosure Requirements Before Application Fee
rules.requirement: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing: (1) whether the housing provider's eligibility criteria include review and consideration of criminal history; and (2) a statement that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies in criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation and mitigating factors.
rules.quoted_span:
Prior to
accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to
the applicant:
(1)   Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing
provider include the review and consideration of criminal history; and
(2)   A statement that the applicant, pursuant to
subsection a. of this section, may provide evidence demonstrating inaccuracies
within the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies before accepting any application fee for all rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rules.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Prohibited Criminal Records for Consideration
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not evaluate an applicant based on: (1) arrests or charges not resulting in conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon; (4) vacated and legally nullified convictions; (5) juvenile adjudications of delinquency; and (6) sealed records, either before or after conditional offer issuance.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rules.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Individualized Assessment Requirement
rules.requirement: Housing provider shall perform an individualized assessment considering: (a) nature and severity of criminal offense; (b) applicant's age at time of offense; (c) time elapsed since offense; (d) applicant-provided evidence of rehabilitation and good conduct; (e) degree to which re-offense would negatively impact tenant/property safety; and (f) whether offense occurred on or was connected to rented/leased property.
rules.quoted_span:
The housing provider shall perform an
individualized assessment of the application in light of the following factors:
(a)   the nature and severity of the criminal offense;
(b)   the age of the applicant at the time of the
occurrence of the criminal offense;
(c)   the time which has elapsed since the occurrence
of the criminal offense;
(d)   any information produced by the applicant, or
produced on the applicant's behalf, in regard to the applicant's rehabilitation
and good conduct since the occurrence of the criminal offense;
(e)   the degree to which the criminal offense, if it
reoccurred, would negatively impact the safety of the housing provider's other
tenants or property; and
(f)   whether the criminal offense occurred on or was
connected to property that was rented or leased by the applicant.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Conditional Offer Withdrawal Standards
rules.requirement: Housing provider may withdraw conditional offer based on criminal record only if provider determines, by preponderance of evidence, that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a
conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing
provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is
necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rules.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Withdrawal Notification and Appeal Rights
rules.requirement: If housing provider withdraws conditional offer, must provide applicant with written notification specifying reasons for withdrawal and opportunity to appeal by providing evidence of inaccuracies in criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation and mitigating factors.
rules.quoted_span:
If a housing provider withdraws a conditional
offer, the housing provider shall provide the applicant with written
notification that includes, with specificity, the reason or reasons for the
withdrawal of the conditional offer and an opportunity to appeal the denial by
providing evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies within
the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rules.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Advertising Restrictions on Criminal History Exclusions
rules.requirement: Housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish any housing advertisement explicitly stating the provider will not consider applicants with criminal history, except for methamphetamine manufacture/production on federally assisted housing premises or lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except
for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.exemptions: Methamphetamine manufacture/production on federally assisted housing; lifetime sex offender registration exclusions are permissible
rules.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Application Form and Inquiry Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing provider shall not print, publish, circulate, display, post, or use any statement, advertisement, publication, sign, application form, record or inquiry expressing directly or indirectly any unlawful limitation, specification or discrimination as to criminal record, except as permitted by the act.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider
shall not print, publish, circulate, issue, display, post, or mail, or cause to
be printed, published, circulated, issued, displayed, posted or mailed any
statement, advertisement, publication or sign, or use any form of application
for the rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion
thereof or make any record or inquiry in connection with the prospective
rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion thereof
which expresses, directly or indirectly, any unlawful limitation, specification
or discrimination as to criminal record, except as permitted by this act and
for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of
methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the
applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex
offender registration program.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Enforcement Complaint Filing Restriction
rules.requirement: Actions alleging violations cannot be initiated in court. Director or applicant/prospective applicant believing housing provider violated provisions may file complaint with Division on Civil Rights.
rules.quoted_span:
An action that alleges a violation of this act
shall not be initiated by any person in court.  The director, or an applicant
or prospective applicant who believes that a housing provider has violated a
provision of this act with respect to that applicant or prospective applicant,
may file a complaint with the division.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rules.sanctions: Administrative penalties through Division on Civil Rights

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Monetary Penalty Tiers
rules.requirement: Housing provider violating provisions liable for: (1) up to $1,000 if no prior violation within 5 years; (2) up to $5,000 if one prior violation within 5 years; (3) up to $10,000 if two or more violations within 7 years.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider who violates a provision of
this act shall be liable for the following applicable penalties:
(1)   an amount not to exceed $1,000 if the housing
provider has not committed any prior violation within the five-year period
ending on the date of the filing of the charge;
(2)   an amount not to exceed $5,000 if the housing
provider has committed one other violation within the five-year period ending
on the date of the filing of the charge; and
(3)   an amount not to exceed $10,000 if the housing
provider has committed two or more other violations within the seven-year
period ending on the date of the filing of the charge.

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Pre-Conditional Offer Criminal Record Inquiry Prohibition
rule.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes inquiries regarding criminal record prior to providing a conditional offer, except for convictions for methamphetamine manufacture/production on federally assisted housing premises or lifetime sex offender registration requirement. Additionally, no oral or written inquiry regarding criminal record is permitted prior to conditional offer.
rule.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program. (2) A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four units in New Jersey
rule.exemptions: Methamphetamine manufacture/production on federally assisted housing premises; lifetime sex offender registration requirement
rule.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Allowable Criminal Records Post-Conditional Offer
rule.requirement: After conditional offer issuance, housing provider may only consider criminal records involving: (1) conviction for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault under N.J.S.2C:14-2, child sexual abuse under N.J.S.2C:24-4(b)(3), or any crime resulting in lifetime sex offender registration; (2) first degree indictable offense issued or completed sentence within 6 years prior; (3) second or third degree indictable offense issued or completed sentence within 4 years prior; or (4) fourth degree indictable offense issued or completed sentence within 1 year prior to conditional offer.
rule.quoted_span: After the issuance of a conditional offer to an applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the applicant's history that: (1) resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry; (2) is for an indictable offense of the first degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; (3) is for an indictable offense of the second or third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; or (4) is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies after conditional offer issued, all rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rule.exemptions: Permanent crimes: murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault under N.J.S.2C:14-2, child sexual abuse under N.J.S.2C:24-4(b)(3), lifetime sex offender registration
rule.sanctions: Monetary penalties up to $1,000 for first violation, $5,000 for one prior violation within 5 years, $10,000 for two or more violations within 7 years

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Applicant Right to Access Information
rule.requirement: Applicant may request within 30 days after withdrawal notice a copy of all information the housing provider relied upon in considering the applicant, including criminal records. Housing provider must provide the information free of charge within 10 days of timely request.
rule.quoted_span: The applicant may request, within 30 days after the housing provider's notice of the withdrawal, that the housing provider afford the applicant a copy of all information that the housing provider relied upon in considering the applicant, including criminal records. rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Criminal Record Dissemination and Use Restrictions
rule.requirement: Unless required by law, housing provider shall not: (1) distribute or disseminate applicant's criminal record to any person not expected to use it for evaluating applicant consistent with the act; or (2) use applicant's criminal record for purposes inconsistent with the act.
rule.quoted_span: Unless otherwise required by law, a housing provider shall not: (1) distribute or disseminate an applicant's criminal record to any person who is not expected to use the criminal record for the purpose of evaluating the applicant in a manner consistent with this act; or (2) use an applicant's criminal record for a purpose that is not consistent with this act.

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Retaliation Prohibition
rule.requirement: No person shall interfere with, restrain, or deny exercise of any right protected under the act. If division determines housing provider engaged in unlawful retaliatory actions in response to applicant filing complaint, each retaliatory action is separate and distinct violation.
rule.quoted_span: A person shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right protected under this act. If the division determines that a housing provider has engaged in one or more unlawful actions against a person with the intent of retaliating for the person's filing of an action against the housing provider pursuant to section 12 of this act, then each unlawful retaliatory action shall be enforced, pursuant to section 12 of this act, as a separate and distinct violation of this act.
rule.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey; applies after complaint filed
rule.sanctions: Each retaliatory action constitutes separate violation; monetary penalties up to $1,000 first violation, $5,000 second, $10,000 for multiple violations

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Mediation and Penalty Structure
rule.requirement: Upon filing of complaint by non-director, division must make good faith effort to notify housing provider and offer mediation within 14 days. No penalty applied if complaint is addressed through mediation. After substantiation finding, director issues monetary penalty and may impose remedial actions.
rule.quoted_span: Upon the filing of a complaint by a person other than the director, the division shall make a good faith effort to notify the housing provider of the alleged violation and offer the housing provider the opportunity to mediate and address the complaint within 14 days of receiving the notice. The division shall not subject a housing provider to any penalty pursuant to subsection c. of this section if the complaint is addressed pursuant to the process identified in this subsection. If the complaint is not resolved in accordance with subsection a. of this section, and the division determines following an investigation that the complaint is substantiated, the director shall issue a monetary penalty against the housing provider and may require the housing provider to take one or more of the actions authorized by subsection d. of this section.
rule.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied 1-4 units in New Jersey
rule.exemptions: Complaints successfully resolved through mediation within 14 days
rule.sanctions: Monetary penalties: up to $1,000 first violation, $5,000 for one prior within 5 years, $10,000 for two+ violations within 7 years; cease and desist; compliance reporting; remedial housing offer; application fee return; payment to applicant up to $1,000

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Remedial Actions Authority
rule.requirement: Director authorized to: (1) require cease and desist, written communication to employees/agents, compliance reporting up to 2 years; (2) if prior violation within 5 years, require good faith remedy efforts including conditional offer or similar unit provision; (3) require application fee return; (4) require payment to applicant up to $1,000.
rule.quoted_span: The director is authorized to require a housing provider to take one or more of the following actions upon a finding that the housing provider has violated a provision of this act: (1) The director may require a housing provider to cease and desist from continuing to violate this act; to communicate in writing to the housing provider's employees and agents their obligations under this act; and to report to the director on the manner of compliance for a period not to exceed two years provided that the housing provider does not commit future violations of the act; (2) If a housing provider has committed at least one other violation of this act within the preceding five-year period, the director may require the housing provider to make a good faith effort to remedy the violation with respect to the applicant when a remedy is possible, by issuing a conditional offer, if the violation has resulted in a failure to issue a conditional offer, or by providing the same or a similar rental dwelling unit to the applicant on the same terms as the prior conditional offer if the same or a similar rental dwelling unit is currently or will become available, if the violation has resulted in the withdrawal of a conditional offer.
rule.sanctions: Cease and desist; written notice to employees; compliance reporting (up to 2 years); conditional offer issuance or similar unit provision; application fee return; payment to applicant ($0-$1,000)

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Landlord Immunity for Criminal Record Rentals
rule.requirement: Landlords subject to the act are immune from civil liability for decision to rent to individuals with criminal record or conviction, or for decision not to engage in criminal background screening, except for immunity of those renting to persons convicted of murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault under N.J.S.2C:14-2, child sexual abuse under N.J.S.2C:24-4(b)(3), or lifetime sex offender registrants.
rule.quoted_span: To encourage residential landlords to provide housing opportunities to formerly incarcerated individuals, landlords subject to the provisions of this act shall be immune from liability in any civil action arising as a result of the landlord's decision to rent to individuals with a criminal record or who were otherwise convicted of a criminal offense, or as a result of a landlord's decision to not engage in a criminal background screening. Nothing in subsection a. of this section shall be construed to affect in any way the immunity from liability conferred by law upon a landlord who rents an apartment to a person with a conviction for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry.
rule.coverage_conditions: All rental properties in New Jersey where landlord decides to rent to or not screen persons with criminal records
rule.exemptions: Immunity does NOT apply to landlords renting to convicted murderers, aggravated sexual assaulters, kidnappers, arsonists, human traffickers, sexual assault violators, child sex abusers, or lifetime sex offender registrants
rule.sanctions: Immunity from civil action except for carved-out serious felony categories
